summary_paragraph: A woman with type I diabetes was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis following poor oral intake and elevated blood glucose levels in the 300s. She developed chest tightness and shortness of breath while at the emergency department with her mother, but cardiac workup including normal troponins and a clear chest X-ray ruled out acute cardiac or pulmonary causes. Her DKA resolved with IV fluids and insulin infusion, transitioning to subcutaneous Lantus and Humalog. She experienced early morning hypoglycemia, prompting a reduction in her evening sliding scale insulin to no more than 5 units. Her chronic conditions, including stage I diabetic nephropathy and hyperlipidemia, were managed with lisinopril and ezetimibe. Psychological factors, including untreated depression and anxiety, were identified as contributors to poor diabetes control, and outpatient psychiatry follow-up was strongly recommended. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated insulin instructions and close follow-up plans.
